text: E1a script 9, probes_score.py (output probes_score.json; probe.py's own --score not rerun, because it writes into the harness's _probe/ and scores the open distinctions against the question files as they stand now). 300 answer files, each with its score file; 0 empty; 283 write their answers in markdown bold ('- **goal:** ...'), which probe.py's line rule does not read, so as filed the goal question is 'missing' in 283 legs and right in 17; open missing 161 (n/a 139); rooms right 6, wrong 9, missing 158 (n/a 127); changed missing 63 (n/a 237); next missing 23 (n/a 277). Re-read by probe.py's own rules with the bold and list marks stripped, against the expected values the harness stored at each close: goal right 298, wrong 2; open right 26, wrong 135 (n/a 139); rooms right 48, wrong 125 (n/a 127); changed right 50, wrong 13 (n/a 237); next right 11, wrong 12 (n/a 277). So most filed misses are the scorer's parse, an instrument defect; the misses left after the re-read (open, rooms) are to be read against the head and the diary in the audit section, a miss either answers being a note. A first run stripped one leading mark only (probes_score.superseded-1.json).

E1a script 10, element_reach.py (output element_reach.json): prior.md section 3's local measure, its element-reach half, computed here at E1a and to be reported in the audit section on composition (section 3), as the PI asked (J, 27 Oct 09:30). The A1 coordinating rule, as coded in _analysis/a1_ends.py, reproduces organizing_end-A1.jsonl exactly: 44,116 turns, all 705 rooms agree; 696 rooms hold a turn, and the nine without are A1's (Lugarix, PokemonSage, ReBoot, Redox, UNLincoln, azores, tetris, watchmen, yerbamate). 5,380 second-order themes hold a coordinating turn. 4,759 of them (88.46 per cent) are reached by a standing element of the frozen model through their third-order placement and its fourth-order theme; with the fifteen candidates, 5,239 (97.38 per cent). Rooms reached in full: 297 of 696 by standing elements, 581 with candidates. Of the 621 themes not reached by a standing element, 28 have no placement; the third-order themes most often unreached are T3-014 (167), T3-017 (115), T3-022 (70), T3-016 (62) and T3-020 (47). This is a structural reach through the tiers, not a reading; the other half (a validated adaptation, or unresolved with its reason) is not computed, so local validation stays not established.

E1a scripts 11 and 12. unplaced.py (output unplaced.json; overlay: scheme_v2.jsonl, assignments_final.jsonl): 151 of 7,844 second-order themes have no third-order placement (36 of them listed in unplaced-B1.jsonl's 58 lines), holding 407 concepts; no concept lacks a theme; two third-order themes no fourth-order theme took: T3-017 'carrying on ordinary sub talk' (334 themes placed) and T3-133 'recovering a hacked sub' (1); all 28 fourth-order themes are gathered by a dimension. What each unplaced theme is gets read in the audit section. manifest.py (output manifest.json): run_manifest.json holds 19 entries, for A1, B2 (8), B3 (2), B4 (5), C2, C5 and D2, each naming a model, seeds and a decoding; the D3 re-check return (adaptations-recheck.jsonl, _fleet_raw/D3v/) has no entry, so its figures have no provenance in the manifest.

E1a script 13, counts_rule.py (output counts_rule.json). The census, twice: rooms.jsonl 705, room folders with a case account 705, the same set; counts.py: census 705, dropped 0, analysed 705; dropped.jsonl empty, so no drop reasons. Stage D4 section 4's four counts by the close-check's own function: 476 in a branch, 0 unadapted, 229 in none, 0 unreturned; sum 705, equal to the analysed set. Ledgers against the head's 'Ledgers (lines)': adjudications 96,568, verdicts 1,029, model history 182, findings 45, elements 45 and arrows 21 agree; tier history disagrees, 1,020 in the head against 1,026 in the file (the 6 D6 naming lines of D6a-01 came after the head's figure; the head is corrected at this close). 361 count phrases in the 18 handbacks are listed for the audit section to check by hand.

E1a script 14, clocks.py (output clocks.json). (1) The coder's created_utc equals the forest item's created_utc for all 115,350 concepts whose item the store holds (the 38 unjoined have none): share 1.0 exact, so the two clocks never disagree; every concept's hour matches its own created_utc (115,388). (2) relations.jsonl: no tool; done by hand in the audit section. (3) Of 598 case accounts with two or more Chronology datings, 237 have datings that step back at least once in the order written. The arrows name few rooms in their records (0 to 4 each: the exemplar rooms), and 14 of the 21 arrows name at least one such room; how far an arrow rests on them is for the audit section, since C2 admits a loop only where one room's datings run the whole way round and no loop is grounded.

E1a script 15, claims.py (output claims.json), the table claims-E1.md will be written from in the audit section. Propositions: 9; carried_by pattern 7, both 2; every one names a rival; each rests on its arrows, all of which give counts with a denominator; every arrow but A11 and A12 beat its base rate (A11 false, A12 not recorded); the arrows themselves cite almost no concept ids (A05, A07 and A14 one each, all resolving), so a words claim's exemplars are to be found through the findings and the accounts by hand. Branches (branches-D5.jsonl): 35; 33 groupings and 2 forms; shared status unresolved 33, supported 2; each branch's confidence sentence ends 'Not established: local validation'.

E1a script 16, diary_transcript.py (output diary_transcript.json). 301 leg closes in _transcripts/INDEX.md, 16 stages; drawn by seed (out/seed.txt), one leg per stage and one more among D6a-09 to D6a-18: A1b-16, B1b-30-p2, B2b-r1, B3a-p2, B4a-05, C1a-07, C2a-02, C3a, C4a, C5c-02-p2, D1a, D2a, D3a-15, D4a-03, D5a-31, D6a-10, D6a-17. Every drawn leg has its transcript. Of their 905 diary lines, 392 are found word for word (the first twelve words) in the leg's transcript; the 513 not found are lines a tool writes from its own arguments (placed 354, opened 92, moves 45, adjudicated 16, asks 6), whose words are not the command typed. Each is to be read against the tool calls in the audit section; no entry is a defect until it is read.

E1a script 17, fleet_figures.py (output fleet_figures.json): the figure lines as the run stated them, stability-B2.md 10, fidelity-B3.md 3, position-B3.md 6, transmission-after-revision-B4.md 10, transmission-B4.md 0 (its figures are not on lines that name them; read by hand), beside FLEET.md section 2's 8 defining lines. The verdict fleet's disagreement rate, recomputed from verdicts-D.jsonl's first return: the readers' verdicts differ in 163 of the 705 rooms with two or more readers (0.2312). That closes the scripts of stage E1 section 1: 17 scripts in out/audit-E1/, each with its output beside it; the readings by hand they call for are the audit sections' work.

E1a closing. The 17 scripts of stage E1 section 1 are in out/audit-E1/, each with its output, results logged one by one above and tabled in notes-E1.md section E1a (with the carried items, QE1-001, licences and slips). prior.md section 3's element-reach half is computed at E1a (audit-E1/element_reach.py) and is reported in the composition section. Answer to the PI's question: I plan eight audit sections, E1b-01 to E1b-08: 01 the quotes and the clocks; 02 the orderings, the counts, coverage and the canvas; 03 the moves and provenance (the D6 proposals, PR-D6-10 against D3a-55, D6a-09 to D6a-18, the manifest, the figures restated); 04 claims against their evidence (claims-E1.md); 05 the diary against the transcript, probes-E1.md and the unplaced; 06 the ledgers, the stories, what a reader was given, departures, defects (100 and 101 reported open), forks, rule 9 (stage section 2); 07 composition and expectations (stage section 3, expectations-E1.md); 08 what bore the load and what the study cannot say (stage sections 6 and 7). Each writes audit-E1/section-NN.md; audit-E1.md is assembled at E1d with stage section 5, the methods paragraph and the composition_status line, which need the reconstruction's fidelity. Head, four Edits (written at E1a; tier history 1,026; QE1-001 open; next E1b-01): 2,997 words, 0 dashes, prose_check 0, links.py all ids resolve. validate.py E1 read before this line (_analysis/e1a_validate_E1.txt): 246 errors, all of one shape, the D4 snaps that list the projection (QE1-001, open); 1 warning, the stage's later outputs not yet written. No .pause. Next: done.sh E1, which will report those 246 lines until QE1-001 is answered.

E1a resumed: QE1-001 answered (J, 27 Oct 18:45 Berlin, through the PI): 'Yes. I would not change the structure of the journey for bookkeeping.' The handler amended check_orderings: a D4 snap counts as a branch cut only where it changed branches.jsonl from the previous snap; one that lists the projection with branches.jsonl unchanged is printed as a finding. My assumption held as the answer states it, so no work changes. Checked by script against the snaps: 82 D4 snaps list the projection, and none changed branches.jsonl from the previous snap. The audit reports them in E1b-02 as the room forms made after the projection by J's ruling, not a recut. notes-E1.md updated (the QE1-001 paragraph); head, two Edits (Questions: none open, QE1-001 answered): 2,996 words, 0 dashes, prose_check 0, links.py all ids resolve. validate.py E1 read before this line (_analysis/e1a_validate_E1-2.txt and a rerun after the edits): 0 errors, 246 findings on the 82 snaps, 1 warning (the stage's later outputs not yet written). No .pause. The plan stands: eight audit sections, E1b-01 to E1b-08, as logged at the first close. Next: done.sh E1.
